step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram represents the Hancom Space cloud infrastructure on AWS. A user accesses the application, which runs on EC2 instances behind an ELB (with Auto Scaling and Spot instances). User file uploads are processed by the main EC2 application server, which stores raw files and preview thumbnails in Amazon S3 and writes file metadata into Amazon Aurora. To optimize performance and reduce database load, user session data is managed via Amazon ElastiCache. Instance logs across the architecture are centralized and monitored using Elasticsearch (Amazon OpenSearch Service).

graph.name: Hancom Space Architecture
graph.notes: Hancom Space uses AWS managed services including S3, Aurora DB, ElastiCache, and Elasticsearch to safely store user files, metadata, and session data while maintaining high availability and centralized log monitoring.

nodes.name: ELB
nodes.notes: Elastic Load Balancer routing incoming client traffic.

nodes.name: EC2
nodes.notes: Main application server handling file processing, thumbnail creation, and business logic.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Object storage for user files and generated thumbnail previews.

nodes.name: Aurora
nodes.notes: Managed relational database storing metadata with 6-copy replication across 3 Availability Zones.

nodes.name: ElastiCache
nodes.notes: Managed cache storing user session data to offload database traffic.

nodes.name: Elasticsearch
nodes.notes: Centralized log management for aggregated monitoring across instances.

nodes.name: Auto Scaling
nodes.notes: Automatically scales application EC2 compute capacity.

nodes.name: EC2 Spot
nodes.notes: Spot compute instances used for cost minimization.

edges.notes: User interacts with the service and uploads files.
Main EC2 stores uploaded files and thumbnails in S3.
Main EC2 writes metadata information to Aurora database.
Main EC2 reads and writes session state from ElastiCache.
Instance logs are pushed to Elasticsearch for centralized troubleshooting.
